newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crudes falter badly in thin volume trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crudes falter badly in thin volume trade.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices faltered Tuesday, deflated by a combination of technical selling in the NYMEX futures market and a lack of refiner demand for new prompt July grade barrels.
July West Texas Intermediate/Cushing wound down afternoon trade some 85 cents lower, around $20.70-80 a barrel.
July/August WTI spreads, or rolls, were steady around minus six cents from the morning.

Traders working the cash sector said refiners wanted to wait before re-entering the search for domestic barrels so soon after filling June needs. July became the prompt barrel month after June business ended Friday.
"You also have the Brent-WTI squeezing a little, and EFPs (Exchange for Physicals) at plus 14-15 cents," said a trader.
Expectations for foreign crude deliveries against July NYMEX positions continued on Tuesday, considering the strong premium cash holds to futures on the EFP value.
More than 2.7 million barrels of foreign crude was delivered against May NYMEX, and just last week more than 2.3 million barrels appeared against June paper positions.
EFPs act as a hedge against getting stuck with non-WTI crudes at delivery time, allowing the EFP buyer or seller to exchange a futures position for a physical position.

At least one confirmed price sold amid the sluggish cash market talk. Traders said Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James changed hands at WTI/Cushing minus five cents, with talk of two other deals at discounts of three and two cents unconfirmed.
Grade talk had West Texas Sour/Midland valued around a $1.45 discount to the benchmark, Eugene Island at WTI/Cushing -$1.55 and July WTI/Cushing Postings Plus around $2.00.
